intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the medieval cobblestone streets of Staré Město, witness the iconic Orloj Astronomical Clock strike the hour with its parade of apostles, and explore the Gothic Týn Church. Join a free walking tour to uncover centuries of Bohemian history, Jewish Quarter stories, and hidden courtyards that shaped Central European culture.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl & Local Street Food Night
experiences.description: Dive into Budapest's legendary ruin bar scene starting at Szimpla Kert, the original ruin pub built inside a crumbling factory. Fuel the night with local street food including lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese), kürtőskalács (chimney cake), and a glass of Unicum herbal liqueur. Experience the raw, eclectic nightlife culture unique to the city.

experiences.name: Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi Baths
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most magnificent thermal bath complexes, a Neo-Baroque palace dating back to 1913. Enjoy outdoor and indoor pools fed by natural hot springs at 38°C, a beloved ritual for locals and travelers alike. The experience offers a perfect blend of relaxation, architecture appreciation, and authentic Hungarian culture.

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex & Malá Strana Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the world's largest ancient castle complex, home to St. Vitus Cathedral, the Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Descend into the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood for a traditional Czech lunch of svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and a cold Pilsner Urquell at a local pivnice (pub). The panoramic views of the Vltava River are unmatched.

experiences.name: Budapest Great Market Hall & Hungarian Cooking Class
experiences.description: Start at the stunning 19th-century Great Market Hall to browse stalls of paprika, salami, Tokaji wine, and handcrafted goods. Then join a small-group Hungarian cooking class where a local chef teaches you to make goulash, stuffed peppers, and chimney cake from scratch using market-fresh ingredients. A deeply immersive taste of Magyar culinary heritage.
experiences.location: Central Market Hall, Fővám tér, Budapest

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at PRG, clear customs, and take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Náměstí Republiky for ~60 CZK (~€2.50), then walk or take tram to your hotel in Staré Město. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely self-guided walk around Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) — admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj), the Church of Our Lady before Týn, and soak in the medieval atmosphere. Free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across Charles Bridge at golden hour for stunning views of Prague Castle and the Vltava River. The bridge is free and magical at dusk. Grab dinner nearby in Malá Strana or back in Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and cheap bite near the hotel — try a 'párek v rohlíku' (Czech hot dog) from a street stand for ~30 CZK (~€1.20) or a fresh bakery roll from a local pekárna.
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33, Old Town) — a beloved Czech pub serving authentic svíčková (beef sirloin) or goulash with bread dumplings for ~180–220 CZK (~€7–9). Great local beer on tap.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Get oriented, rest after travel, and enjoy the magic of Old Town without rushing. Buy a 24-hour public transport pass (~120 CZK) for easy tram and metro access.

day_by_day.morning: Start with Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle in the world. Take Tram 22 uphill to save energy. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane (cobblestone alley of tiny houses). Budget entry ticket ~250 CZK (~€10) for Circuit B. Arrive early (~9:00) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through Malá Strana (Lesser Town), exploring its charming baroque streets, Wallenstein Garden (free entry), and the Church of St. Nicholas. Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore Josefov, Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Stroll the streets for free — museum entry is optional (~350 CZK if interested).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods by tram for a more local, less touristy evening. Explore Náměstí Míru square and the surrounding café-lined streets.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy (Vítězná 5, Malá Strana) for a budget morning pastry and coffee ~80–120 CZK, OR grab a croissant from a nearby pekárna for ~30 CZK.
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Dlouhá 39) — a butcher-deli hybrid with incredible open-faced sandwiches and burgers for ~100–150 CZK (~€4–6). Very local and very good.
meals.dinner: Hospůdka Na Hradbách or a local pub in Žižkov — try svíčková, roast pork knee (vepřové koleno), or fried cheese (smažený sýr) for ~150–200 CZK (~€6–8). Order a half-liter of Czech pilsner for ~40–50 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle can take 3–4 hours. Wear comfortable shoes — there's significant walking and cobblestones. September weather is typically mild (15–20°C), so bring a light jacket for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) — a grand boulevard central to Czech history. Walk its full length, visit the National Museum (free on first Sunday, otherwise ~200 CZK — check schedule) at the top, and absorb the historical significance of the 1968 and 1989 revolutions. Continue to the nearby Mucha Museum (~240 CZK) if you're interested in Art Nouveau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Vyšehrad Fortress — a lesser-known gem with panoramic views of the Vltava River, a stunning neo-Gothic basilica, and a cemetery where Czech legends like Dvořák and Smetana are buried. Entry to the grounds is FREE; basilica interior ~50 CZK. Take Tram 7 or 18 from the city center. Peaceful and far fewer tourists than Prague Castle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town for a final Prague evening. Walk the illuminated Old Town Square one last time. Consider a live jazz or classical music performance — many affordable concerts (~300–500 CZK) are held in historic churches throughout the city.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre (Národní 22) — a historic grand café popular since 1902. Try their breakfast set for ~120–180 CZK. A true Prague institution.
meals.lunch: Grab food near Vyšehrad — bring a picnic from Albert supermarket (affordable sandwiches, fruit, drinks for ~80–100 CZK) and eat with a view of the river.
meals.dinner: Restaurace U Fleků (Křemencova 11) — Prague's oldest brewery (founded 1499). Dark lager brewed on-site. Order the pork knee or goulash. Budget ~250–350 CZK for food and drinks. A true Prague bucket-list experience.

day_by_day.notes: This is your last full day in Prague. Consider buying souvenirs from local markets rather than tourist shops — prices are significantly lower. Pack your bags tonight for the early Budapest journey tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Prague hotel and take the RegioJet or FlixBus from Prague to Budapest — the most budget-friendly option (~€15–25, ~7 hours). Book in advance for best prices. Buses depart from Florenc Bus Station (metro B: Florenc). Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside through the window.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest (Keleti or Népliget station, depending on route) in the early-to-mid afternoon. Check into your Budapest accommodation. Take the metro or tram to explore the Pest side of the city. Walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) for stunning views of Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and Parliament. All free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) at Fővám tér — even if it's closing time, walk around the exterior and nearby streets. Then head to the Jewish Quarter / Ruin Bar District (VII. district) for an evening stroll through the eclectic streets.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick pastry (kürtőskalács or a croissant) from a Prague bakery before departure, or eat at the bus station café for ~80–120 CZK.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the bus journey — bread, cheese, fruit from a Prague supermarket (~100 CZK). Saves money and time.
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food (Kazinczy utca, Jewish Quarter) — Budapest's famous outdoor street food garden with multiple vendors. Try a lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) for ~800–1200 HUF (~€2–3.50), or a burger/grilled dish. Very local, very affordable.

day_by_day.notes: Travel day — keep it relaxed. Book the bus ticket at least 3–5 days in advance for best budget prices. Download the BKK app or buy a 24-hour Budapest transit pass (~2,500 HUF) upon arrival. Exchange some cash to HUF — many local spots prefer cash.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Buda Castle District — take the free Sikló (funicular) walk-up or hike up Castle Hill. Explore the Fisherman's Bastion (free exterior, ~1,000 HUF for tower access) for some of the best panoramic views of Budapest and the Danube. Visit Matthias Church (~2,000 HUF entry). The whole area is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Castle Hill and cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot — free and iconic. On the Pest side, walk up Andrássy Avenue (another UNESCO site) toward Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — completely free and spectacular. Visit City Park (Városliget) and see Vajdahunyad Castle exterior for free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and explore the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (largest in Europe) — exterior is free; interior entry ~4,000 HUF (~€11) if interested. Then wander the Jewish Quarter's ruin bars for drinks.

meals.breakfast: Molnár's Kürtőskalács (multiple locations) — grab a fresh chimney cake for ~600–800 HUF (~€1.50–2). A quintessential Budapest street breakfast.
meals.lunch: Hummus Bar (Paulay Ede utca 2) — generous portions of hummus, falafel, and pita for ~1,500–2,000 HUF (~€4–5.50). Very popular with locals and great value.
meals.dinner: Kőleves (Kazinczy utca 41) — a cozy Jewish Quarter restaurant with hearty Hungarian dishes like goulash soup, stuffed cabbage, and chicken paprikash for ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€7–10) per main. Excellent atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means the Great Market Hall may be busier — consider visiting Sunday morning instead. Fisherman's Bastion is most magical at sunrise or sunset. September in Budapest is typically warm (18–24°C) — perfect for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — it opens Sunday mornings and is a feast for the senses. Browse fresh produce, Hungarian paprika, salami, pickles, folk crafts, and lángos on the upper floor. Great for affordable souvenir shopping. Budget ~1,000–2,000 HUF for snacks and browsing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Hungarian Parliament Building from the outside along the Danube (stunning, free). If budget allows, book a guided interior tour (~6,000 HUF / ~€16 for EU citizens, or ~3,000 HUF for EU students — book online in advance at parlament.hu). Then walk to St. Stephen's Basilica — exterior free; climb the dome for panoramic city views (~800 HUF).
day_by_day.evening: Experience a Budapest thermal bath — Széchenyi Baths in City Park is the most famous and grand (~6,500–8,000 HUF / ~€17–22 for 3-hour entry). Alternatively, Rudas Baths (more local feel, ~4,500 HUF for weekday entry) is more budget-friendly. A uniquely Hungarian experience not to be missed.

meals.breakfast: Lángos from the Great Market Hall upper floor — ~800–1,200 HUF (~€2–3.50). The ultimate Budapest breakfast experience.
meals.lunch: Belvárosi Lugas (Irányi utca 8) — a hidden local gem with traditional Hungarian lunch menus (napi menü) for ~1,800–2,500 HUF (~€5–7) including soup and main. Look for 'napi menü' signs on weekdays for the best deals.
meals.dinner: Menza (Liszt Ferenc tér 2) — stylish retro-communist-era design with modern Hungarian cuisine. Mains ~2,500–4,000 HUF (~€7–11). Try the goulash or pörkölt (Hungarian beef stew). Great location on a lively square.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Parliament tour online in advance — slots fill up quickly, especially on weekends. The thermal bath experience is a must-do in Budapest — bring a towel or rent one on-site (~300–500 HUF). Sunday is a great day for markets and a slower pace.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) — hike up (free) for the best panoramic views of Budapest, the Danube, and all seven bridges. Visit the Citadella fortress at the top (free exterior). The hike takes ~30–45 minutes and is very rewarding. Start early to avoid heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) at Heroes' Square — one of Central Europe's finest art collections with works by Raphael, El Greco, and Rembrandt (~3,200 HUF / ~€9, free on first Sunday of month). Alternatively, explore the Hungarian National Museum (~1,600 HUF) for a deep dive into Hungarian history and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Take a free sunset walk along the Danube Promenade on the Pest side — the Parliament and Buda Castle lit up at night is absolutely breathtaking. Consider a budget Danube cruise (~3,000–5,000 HUF / ~€8–14) for a different perspective — many evening options available from Vigadó tér.

meals.breakfast: Auguszt Cukrászda (Kossuth Lajos utca 14) — a historic Budapest patisserie open since 1870. Enjoy a coffee and pastry for ~800–1,200 HUF (~€2–3.50).
meals.lunch: Falafel Faloda (Paulay Ede utca 53) — budget-friendly falafel wraps and plates for ~1,200–1,800 HUF (~€3–5). Popular with students and locals.
meals.dinner: Rosenstein (Mosonyi utca 3) — a legendary family-run restaurant near Keleti Station serving traditional Hungarian-Jewish cuisine. Try the goose liver or stuffed cabbage. Mains ~3,000–4,500 HUF (~€8–12). Book a table in advance — it's popular.

day_by_day.notes: Gellért Hill is best in the morning before it gets busy. Wear sturdy shoes for the hike. Monday may mean some museums are closed — always check opening hours in advance. This is your second-to-last day, so prioritize any remaining must-see sights.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — revisit any favorite spots or explore the Váci utca shopping street (pedestrian zone) for last-minute souvenirs. Better yet, head to the Ecseri Flea Market (Nagykőrösi út 156, open Mon–Fri 8:00–16:00, Sat 6:00–15:00) for authentic Hungarian antiques, vintage items, and unique souvenirs at local prices — take Bus 54 from Boráros tér.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight/train, use this time to pack, check out, and head to the airport or station. Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport is accessible by Bus 100E (~900 HUF direct from Deák Ferenc tér, ~35 min) — the most budget-friendly airport transfer option.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most beautiful and historically rich capitals.

meals.breakfast: New York Café (Erzsébet körút 9–11) — splurge on a coffee in the world's most beautiful café (~1,500–2,000 HUF for coffee and pastry). A once-in-a-trip treat for your last morning.
meals.lunch: Quick and budget-friendly — grab a döner kebab or gyros wrap from a local fast-food spot near your accommodation for ~1,000–1,500 HUF (~€3–4), or pick up snacks from a Spar or Aldi for the journey home.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or pack snacks from a local supermarket to save money on travel day.

day_by_day.notes: Bus 100E to the airport is far cheaper than a taxi (~8,000–12,000 HUF). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the journey and check-in. Keep some HUF for the bus ticket — exact change preferred. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Airport Express bus or metro (Line A) to Staré Město. Journey takes approximately 45–60 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique hotel in Staré Město. Once settled, take a gentle orientation stroll through Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) — admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj), the Church of Our Lady before Týn, and the Jan Hus Memorial. Let the medieval atmosphere wash over you at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Wander across the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův most) at dusk for golden-hour views of Prague Castle and the Vltava River. Enjoy your first Czech dinner nearby in Malá Strana or back in Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near Old Town Square after check-in — try a traditional Czech open-faced sandwich (chlebíček) from a local deli or bakery like Nákladní or a nearby café.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved mid-range Czech gastropub serving perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell and classic dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or roast pork with dumplings. Budget ~€15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestones. The Astronomical Clock chimes on the hour; try to catch it around 5 or 6 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) exploration — take the tram (No. 22) or walk up from Charles Bridge. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, the Story of Prague Castle exhibition, and stroll Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička), the charming row of tiny medieval houses. Arrive early (around 9 AM) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) and explore its baroque streets, hidden courtyards, and the beautiful Wallenstein Garden (free entry, open afternoons). Cross back over Charles Bridge and visit the Old Town Hall Tower for panoramic rooftop views over the red rooftops of Prague.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) at a relaxed pace — walk through its atmospheric streets and admire the synagogue exteriors. Enjoy dinner in the Josefov or Old Town area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — try Café Louvre-style pastries and coffee. Budget ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café inside or near Prague Castle — Café Poet or a local spot in Malá Strana. Try trdelník (chimney cake) as a street snack while walking. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Café Savoy in Malá Strana — a stunning neo-Renaissance interior with excellent Czech and Central European cuisine. Try the beef goulash or duck confit. Budget ~€18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle complex in the world — wear good walking shoes. Buy a combined ticket (Circuit B or C) online in advance to skip queues. Wallenstein Garden closes in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery and the Jewish Museum complex (Josefov) — one of the most moving and historically significant sites in Central Europe. The layered graves and the Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting memorial walls are deeply affecting. Book tickets online in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods — two authentic, less-touristy Prague districts. Explore the Art Nouveau apartment buildings, visit the striking Žižkov Television Tower (with its crawling baby sculptures), and browse local cafés and boutiques. Take the metro or tram from the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town for a classical music concert — Prague is famous for chamber music performances in historic venues. Check listings for concerts at the Municipal House (Obecní dům) or the Klementinum Mirror Chapel. Enjoy a pre-concert dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Eska Bakery in Karlín (slightly outside Old Town but worth it) — sourdough breads, pastries, and excellent coffee. Budget ~€7–10.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Vinohrady at Café Slávia-style bistro or try Maitrea — a vegetarian restaurant with creative Czech-inspired dishes in a beautiful wooden interior near Old Town. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Čestr — a modern Czech steakhouse near the National Theatre serving premium cuts and local craft beer. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Museum ticket covers multiple sites — plan at least 2–2.5 hours. September evenings in Prague can be cool (12–18°C), so bring a light jacket for the concert.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or morning exploration of Vyšehrad — the ancient fortress and cemetery perched above the Vltava River, with stunning views and the graves of Czech luminaries like Dvořák and Smetana. Far less crowded than Prague Castle and equally atmospheric. Take the metro (Line C, Vyšehrad station).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day to Budapest. Take the RegioJet or FlixBus from Prague Florenc bus station, or the EC train from Praha hlavní nádraží (Main Train Station) — journey is approximately 6–7 hours by train or 7 hours by bus. Arrive in Budapest by early evening. Check in to your Budapest accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest and take a gentle first-night stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side — the illuminated Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and Parliament Building at night are absolutely breathtaking. A perfect low-key introduction to Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Prague hotel or a nearby café before checkout. Budget ~€6–9.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or grab food at Prague's Florenc bus/train station — local sandwiches, fruit, and snacks for the journey. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: First dinner in Budapest at Hungarikum Bisztró near the Great Market Hall — hearty Hungarian classics like goulash soup, chicken paprikash, and lángos in a warm, welcoming setting. Budget ~€15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book train or bus tickets in advance — RegioJet offers comfortable seats with onboard service at mid-range prices (~€20–35 one way). The train is more scenic and comfortable for this journey. Confirm Budapest accommodation check-in time.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Buda Castle District — take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up from Clark Ádám Square or walk up the castle hill. Visit the Royal Palace (Hungarian National Gallery), Matthias Church, and the Fisherman's Bastion — one of the most photogenic spots in all of Europe with sweeping panoramic views over the Danube and the Hungarian Parliament.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge on foot into Pest. Explore the elegant Lipótváros (Leopold Town) district — stroll past the magnificent Hungarian Parliament Building (exterior), visit St. Stephen's Basilica (climb the dome for city views), and browse the upscale Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Ruin Bar scene in the Jewish Quarter (District VII) — Budapest's famous ruin bars are built in abandoned pre-war buildings and courtyards. Start with a drink at Szimpla Kert, the original and most iconic ruin bar, open every night with a fantastic atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Budapest café — try Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square, one of the city's most historic and elegant coffee houses. Enjoy pastries and coffee. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Fisherman's Bastion at a local spot — try Halászbástya Restaurant for Hungarian fish soup (halászlé) or grab a kürtőskalács (chimney cake) as a street snack. Budget ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Borkonyha Winekitchen — a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant offering creative Hungarian cuisine paired with excellent local wines. Reservations strongly recommended. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday at Szimpla Kert can be very busy — arrive before 9 PM for a better experience. The Fisherman's Bastion is free to enter (the terraces have a small fee). Wear comfortable shoes for the castle hill cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — Budapest's stunning 19th-century iron-and-glass market hall, especially vibrant on Sunday mornings. Browse stalls of paprika, salami, pickles, embroidery, and local produce. Perfect for picking up food souvenirs. Then visit the nearby Hungarian National Museum for a deep dive into Hungarian history from Roman times to the present.
day_by_day.afternoon: Thermal bath experience at Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park — Budapest's largest and most famous outdoor thermal bath complex, with its iconic yellow neo-baroque architecture. Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the naturally hot mineral waters. Rent a towel and locker on-site. A quintessential Budapest experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore City Park (Városliget) and Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — the grand Millennium Monument with statues of the seven Magyar chieftains and Hungarian kings is especially atmospheric at dusk. Enjoy dinner in the Andrássy Avenue area.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Great Market Hall itself — fresh lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) is a classic Sunday morning street food. Budget ~€4–6.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the market or pack snacks from the market stalls. Alternatively, try Kőleves (Stone Soup) in the Jewish Quarter — a cozy, mid-range bistro with excellent Hungarian comfort food. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Menza on Liszt Ferenc Square — a retro-chic Hungarian restaurant with a beautiful terrace, serving updated Hungarian classics in a lively neighborhood. Budget ~€18–24 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Széchenyi Baths are open daily; buy tickets online in advance on weekends to avoid queues (~€22–28 for a standard entry with locker). Bring flip-flops and a swimsuit. The market hall closes early on Sundays (around 3 PM), so go in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the most spectacular Gothic Revival buildings in the world and the largest building in Hungary. Guided tours run regularly and take you through the Grand Staircase, the Dome Hall, and the Crown Jewels. Book tickets online well in advance as tours sell out. Arrive early.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Margaret Island (Margit-sziget) — a peaceful, car-free island in the middle of the Danube, accessible by tram or on foot via Margaret Bridge. Stroll through its gardens, visit the medieval monastery ruins, the musical fountain, and the Japanese Garden. Rent a four-wheeled pedal car for fun. A lovely contrast to the city's grand architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Danube River Cruise — take a 1–2 hour evening cruise on the Danube for unparalleled views of the illuminated Parliament, Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and Gellért Hill. Several operators run departures from Vigadó Square. A magical way to see Budapest from the water.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation or a nearby café. Try Auguszt Cukrászda — a historic Hungarian pastry shop with excellent rétes (strudel) and coffee. Budget ~€6–9.
meals.lunch: Lunch on Margaret Island — bring a picnic from a nearby supermarket or grab food from one of the island's casual eateries. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Farewell Budapest dinner at Costes Downtown — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering refined Hungarian and European cuisine in an elegant setting. A special splurge for the last Budapest evening. Budget ~€45–65 per person (set menu).

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours are very popular — book 2–4 weeks in advance at jegymester.hu. The evening cruise typically costs €15–25 per person; choose a departure around 7:30–8 PM for the best illuminated views. Dress smartly for Costes Downtown.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) for the best panoramic views of the entire city. Walk up the hill (30–40 minutes) or take a taxi to the Citadella fortress at the top. The view of the Danube, both bridges, Parliament, and Buda Castle from here is arguably the finest in the city. Visit the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor) at the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration of the Belváros (Inner City) — browse the stylish Váci Street for souvenirs, visit the elegant Párisi Udvar (Paris Arcade), a stunning Art Nouveau shopping arcade now converted into a luxury hotel (free to enter and admire). Stop at a final Hungarian pastry shop for a last slice of Dobos torte or Esterházy cake.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for transfer and check-in. The airport is approximately 30–40 minutes from the city center by taxi or Airport Shuttle (100E bus to Kőbánya-Kispest metro, then metro to city center in reverse).

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Gerbeaud or a local café near your accommodation — enjoy one last Hungarian coffee and pastry. Budget ~€7–10.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a relaxed spot in Belváros — try Frici Papa Kifőzdéje, a legendary no-frills Hungarian canteen serving hearty, home-style dishes at very low prices. A true local institution. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or light snacks before your flight — grab a final Hungarian beer and sandwich at the airport. Budget ~€10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and plan your airport transfer accordingly. If you have a late flight, consider storing luggage at the hotel and spending extra time in the city. Budapest Airport taxi fares are regulated — use official taxis (Főtaxi) or pre-book a transfer. A wonderful 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent capitals!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury car service (Mercedes E-Class or similar) to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge, admiring the Baroque statues and panoramic views of the Vltava River. Continue to Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the twin-spired Týn Church. Explore the winding medieval lanes at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a celebrated Prague fine-dining restaurant — Field Restaurant (Michelin-recognized, modern Czech cuisine with seasonal tasting menus) is an excellent first-night choice, just steps from Old Town Square. After dinner, take a scenic night walk along the illuminated Charles Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light snack or coffee upon arrival at the hotel — many boutique Old Town hotels offer a welcome refreshment at check-in.
meals.lunch: Late lunch / early afternoon snack at Café Savoy or Lokál Dlouhááá — classic Czech open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky) and premium Czech pilsner to ease into the city.
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant (U Milosrdných 12, Staré Město) — 5-course tasting menu with Czech wine pairing. Reservations strongly recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally relaxed given the 13:00 arrival. Prioritize unpacking and light exploration over packed sightseeing. Confirm Day 2–8 restaurant reservations with your hotel concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) experience — the largest ancient castle in the world. Begin with St. Vitus Cathedral, then explore the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička). Hire a private licensed guide for a 3-hour deep-dive into the history of Bohemian kings and Habsburg rule.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) — explore the Baroque gardens of Wallenstein Palace and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the Church of St. Nicholas (Malá Strana). Cross back over Charles Bridge and visit the Franz Kafka Museum in Josefov (the historic Jewish Quarter). Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery and the Spanish Synagogue.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague is world-renowned for intimate evening concerts held in historic venues. Options include the Municipal House (Obecní dům) or a private palace concert. Afterward, cocktails at the rooftop bar of Hotel Aria or Augustine Hotel.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at your boutique hotel — most premium Old Town properties offer an elaborate continental and hot breakfast spread.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Coda Restaurant (Hotel Aria, Malá Strana) — elegant terrace with views over Baroque gardens; refined European cuisine.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise (Michelin-starred, Haštalská 18) — 11-course Czech heritage tasting menu. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle opens at 09:00. Arrive early to beat crowds. The Jewish Quarter museums sell combination tickets — purchase online in advance. September evenings can be cool; bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — Prague's elegant residential districts with Art Nouveau architecture. Visit the iconic Žižkov Television Tower (with the crawling baby sculptures by David Černý) and enjoy panoramic views from the observation deck. Wander the farmers' market at náměstí Míru if it falls on a market day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square, recently renovated to world-class standards — explore Czech natural history and national identity. Then take a private walking tour of Wenceslas Square with a historian-guide, covering the 1968 Prague Spring and the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Prague National Theatre (Národní divadlo) — opera, ballet, or drama in one of Europe's most beautiful Neo-Renaissance theatres. Book premium seats in advance.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel, followed by a specialty coffee at EMA Espresso Bar (one of Prague's top third-wave coffee destinations).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Eska (Pernerova 49, Karlín district) — acclaimed modern Czech bistro with wood-fired dishes and craft ferments; a short taxi ride from the hotel.
meals.dinner: Pre-theatre dinner at Kampa Park Restaurant (Na Kampě 8b, Malá Strana) — riverside fine dining with stunning views of Charles Bridge; contemporary European cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: National Theatre tickets for September should be booked 4–6 weeks in advance. Vinohrady is best explored on foot or by tram — your hotel concierge can arrange a private car if preferred.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora (1.5 hours from Prague by private car) — a UNESCO World Heritage medieval silver-mining town. Visit the hauntingly beautiful Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), decorated with the bones of 40,000 people, followed by the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara (Chrám sv. Barbory).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague. Check out of your Prague boutique hotel and transfer to Prague Main Station (Hlavní nádraží) for the afternoon Regiojet or Leo Express premium train to Budapest Keleti Station (approximately 7 hours) — or opt for a private luxury car transfer for a more exclusive experience (approx. 5.5 hours via motorway). Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest. Private transfer to your luxury hotel in Budapest (recommend Buda Castle District or Andrássy Avenue area). Light evening walk along the Danube embankment to see the illuminated Chain Bridge and Parliament building from the Pest side.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at your Prague boutique hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora — try Restaurace Pivovar Kutná Hora for traditional Bohemian cuisine and locally brewed beer in a historic brewery setting.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Onyx Restaurant (Vörösmarty tér 7–8) — Michelin-starred Hungarian fine dining with a contemporary tasting menu. Ideal first-night Budapest experience.

day_by_day.notes: Kutná Hora is best visited on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. Confirm Budapest hotel check-in time given the late afternoon/evening arrival. Luggage can be stored at Prague hotel during the day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill — a UNESCO World Heritage site. Visit the Royal Palace (Hungarian National Gallery), Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) with its stunning Zsolnay ceramic roof tiles, and the Fishermen's Bastion (Halászbástya) for breathtaking panoramic views over the Danube and Pest. Hire a private guide for a 3-hour historical tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi lánchíd) on foot to the Pest side. Explore the Hungarian Parliament Building exterior (book an interior guided tour in advance — one of the most magnificent parliament buildings in the world). Walk along the Danube Promenade and visit the moving Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial.
day_by_day.evening: Thermal bath evening experience — Budapest is the city of thermal baths. Book a private evening session at Széchenyi Thermal Bath or the more exclusive Gellért Thermal Bath. Afterward, dinner in the Jewish Quarter (Erzsébetváros).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Budapest luxury hotel — many top properties (Four Seasons Gresham Palace, Aria Hotel Budapest) offer exceptional breakfast spreads.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Halászbástya Restaurant — elegant dining with unrivaled views of the Danube from Fishermen's Bastion terrace; Hungarian and European cuisine.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Costes Restaurant (Ráday utca 4) — Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant; innovative Hungarian cuisine with an outstanding wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament interior tours must be booked online in advance at www.parlament.hu. Széchenyi and Gellért baths offer private cabin rentals and VIP packages — book ahead for Saturday evenings. September water temperatures are still pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's stunning 19th-century iron-and-glass market hall. Browse artisan stalls selling Hungarian paprika, foie gras, Tokaji wine, and handcrafted goods. Purchase premium Hungarian food souvenirs. Then explore the Jewish Quarter — visit the Great Synagogue (Dohány Street Synagogue), the largest in Europe, and the Hungarian Jewish Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Andrássy Avenue exploration — Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House (Operaház) on a guided interior tour (even if not attending a performance, the interior is extraordinary). Explore the House of Terror Museum (Terror Háza) — a powerful and sobering museum documenting Hungary's Nazi and Communist occupations.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — one of the finest opera venues in Europe; September marks the start of the new season. Book premium box seats. Pre-show champagne in the gilded foyer.

meals.breakfast: Sunday brunch at New York Café (Erzsébet körút 9–11) — arguably the most beautiful café in the world; a legendary Budapest institution with ornate frescoed ceilings and exceptional brunch service.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at one of the Great Market Hall's upper-floor stalls — try lángos (Hungarian fried dough with sour cream and cheese) for an authentic local snack experience.
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Borkonyha Winekitchen (Sas utca 3) — Michelin Bib Gourmand; outstanding Hungarian wine selection with creative seasonal dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Opera tickets for the September season open approximately 2–3 months in advance — book as early as possible. New York Café Sunday brunch is extremely popular; reservations are essential. The House of Terror has emotionally intense content.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Danube Bend (Dunakanyar) — one of Central Europe's most scenic landscapes. Private car to Visegrád (medieval royal citadel with sweeping Danube views), then Esztergom (Hungary's first capital city, dominated by the massive Esztergom Basilica — the largest church in Hungary). Private guide recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Szentendre — a charming Baroque artists' town on the Danube with Serbian Orthodox churches, art galleries, and artisan workshops. Visit the Open-Air Ethnographic Museum (Skanzen) for a fascinating insight into traditional Hungarian village life across different regions. Return to Budapest by private car.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube — book a private luxury boat charter for a 2-hour evening cruise past the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and Gellért Hill. Champagne and canapés on board. Conclude the evening with cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Aria Hotel Budapest or High Note SkyBar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Szentendre at Rab Ráby Restaurant — a historic riverside restaurant serving traditional Hungarian cuisine in a beautifully preserved Baroque setting.
meals.dinner: Farewell Budapest dinner at Stand Restaurant (Széll Kálmán tér 1) — Michelin-starred; Chef Széll Tamás's celebrated modern Hungarian cuisine using heritage ingredients and techniques.

day_by_day.notes: The Danube Bend day trip covers approximately 120km by car. A private driver is strongly recommended for flexibility. The Danube cruise should be booked 2–3 days in advance through your hotel concierge or a specialist operator (e.g., Legenda Cruises or a private charter).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit Margaret Island (Margit-sziget), a peaceful green oasis in the middle of the Danube. Stroll through the rose gardens, visit the medieval monastery ruins, and enjoy the tranquility before departure. Alternatively, revisit a favorite neighborhood for last-minute souvenir shopping on Váci Street or in the Design District around Ráday Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely hotel checkout (arrange late checkout with your hotel if flight permits). Final coffee and pastry at Gerbeaud Café (Vörösmarty tér 7) — Budapest's most iconic historic coffeehouse, established in 1858. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD) for departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on an extraordinary 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's greatest imperial capitals.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at your Budapest luxury hotel — savor it unhurriedly.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Gerbeaud Café or a light meal at the airport's premium lounge (Budapest Airport has a well-appointed VIP lounge for business and first-class travelers).
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at destination upon return.

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout (13:00–14:00) from your hotel to maximize the final morning without luggage pressure. Budapest airport is approximately 30–40 minutes from the city center; allow 2.5 hours before departure for a comfortable experience. Consider purchasing a bottle of premium Tokaji Aszú wine as the quintessential Hungarian luxury souvenir.
